---
title: "Upgrading and rolling back"
---

## What is pinned

Every image is pinned to a release tag or, where a project publishes no
releases, to a digest. The current set:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| I-SPI | `1.1.1` |
| i-spi-compute API and worker | `1.1.0` (curveRcore 0.7.0, curveRfreq 0.5.2, curveRbayes 0.5.2, curveRweights 0.3.0, CmdStan 2.40.0) |
| Database schema (calib schema) | `0.7.0` |

The [automated checks](checks.html) fail if an ImmunoPlex image is not pinned,
or if the Kubernetes manifests and the Compose file use different versions.

I-SPI's About page (in its sidebar) shows the running I-SPI version, the
database's calib schema version, and which compute releases produced the
stored results.

## Upgrading

1. Read what changed: I-SPI's
   [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/immunoplex/i-spi/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md),
   and for i-spi-compute its [tags](https://github.com/immunoplex/i-spi-compute/tags)
   and the README in `worker/migrations/`.
2. **If the new i-spi-compute release brings a new calib schema version**,
   apply its migration to the existing database before starting the new
   worker. Migrations are in i-spi-compute's
   [`worker/migrations/`](https://github.com/immunoplex/i-spi-compute/tree/main/worker/migrations),
   with instructions in that folder's README. The table `schema_version`
   records which version the database holds.
3. Change the image tags in the manifests (`i-spi.yml`, `i-spi-compute.yml`,
   and `i-spi-compute-sim.yml` if used) and apply them. On the
   [local stack](install-local.html), change `local/docker-compose.yml` and run
   `docker compose up -d`.
4. Check the About page.

The schema files in [`db/`](database-schema.html) are only for a new, empty
database. Do not load them into a database that already has data.

## Rolling back

Apply the previous image tags. A rollback of I-SPI or of the worker alone does
not touch the database.

The migrations so far only add tables, columns and views, so older images keep
working with a newer schema: I-SPI 1.0.0 runs against calib schema 0.7.0. A
migration cannot be undone by changing images; restore from a database backup
if you need the old schema itself. Take a `pg_dump` before every migration.
